scores.evidence: This architecture is production-ready and handles enterprise-scale requirements while maintaining developer experience and operational simplicity.
scores.rationale: No assumptions stated about scale, team, jurisdictions or budget; dashboard shows invented figures and the plan asserts production-readiness unsupported.
Some retry/dunning and signature verification, but no handling of duplicate or out-of-order webhooks, crash between charge and record, late usage, disputes, or corruption.
Has CI/CD, blue-green deploy, metrics and alerts, but no migration across per-tenant databases, no rollback procedure, ownership or incident process, and the burden is large.
Costs essentially ignored; per-tenant databases, Kubernetes, Kafka, Elasticsearch, fallback provider and VPC-per-tenant imply heavy cost with no remark.
A gateway abstraction is mentioned, but tenancy model, ID scheme, money format and price versioning one-way decisions are unexamined and inconsistent.
Microservices, Kafka, Elasticsearch, SMS, HIPAA, SOC2, VPC per tenant, fallback provider are speculative, while essentials like ledger and reconciliation are missing.
Lots of code but no build order, no first steps, and most real decisions left open (language, queue, tenancy model).
